subject: Transfer Impact Assessment: controller data-flow verification for Medra Health
messages:
From: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medra.tech>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com
Cc: DataPrivacy@medra.tech; liam.oconnor@medra.tech
Date: 2028-03-22T09:17:00Z
Subject: TIA — verification of controller data flows and vendors

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of Medra Health's procurement process we need to complete a short Transfer Impact Assessment and confirm the operational controls for any EU->US transfers. Can you please: 

- Confirm where patient identifiers and pseudonymized event logs may transit (regions, services).
- Provide an updated data-flow diagram that highlights which components are controllers vs processors for the onboarding scope.
- Confirm whether Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated would be used for Medra; if Private, note KMS/HSM integration options and whether keys remain in-customer-control.
- Share any SCC extracts you can provide that show subprocessors involved in cross-border processing.

We are on a tight review timeline for our DPIA; ideally we get this by EOD Thursday (2028-03-23). Please attach any exportable logs or retention policy snippets that can help our security team validate data residency.

Appreciate it — if it's easier we can hop on a 30-min call.

Best,
Carlos
Privacy Lead, Medra Health

[Medra Health — procurement reference: MED-ONB-728]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
To: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medra.tech>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-03-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: TIA — verification of controller data flows and vendors

Carlos — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial data-flow diagram and a short evidence bundle that addresses the bullets. High level answers below; details in the attachments.

- EU->US transfers: For hosted Redwood API calls by default traffic may traverse our us-west and eu-west regions depending on routing policy. For Medra we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated to avoid cross-region routing; Private keeps the control plane in your VPC and supports customer-managed KMS.
- Controller vs processor: Medra remains the controller for patient identifiers; Redwood acts as processor for model inference, logging, and metrics. See annotated diagram (TIA_data_flow_diagram_v2.pdf).
- KMS/HSM and keys: Private supports bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed key wrapping. Keys can be kept under customer control; we list options in the attachment.
- SCC extracts & subprocessors: included SCCs_signed_extract.pdf (redactions applied).
- Logs/retention: exported sample logs included (redwood-logs-export-20280301.csv) and retention policy excerpt in the PDF.

Next steps: Rishi and Kim will answer the technical questions about edge routing and KV cache exports below. If that looks good I can also schedule a 30-min call with Medra's DPIA team tomorrow morning (Mar 23).

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0123
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: TIA_data_flow_diagram_v2.pdf; SCCs_signed_extract.pdf; redwood-logs-export-20280301.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com; Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medra.tech>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-03-22T13:18:00Z
Subject: Re: TIA — verification of controller data flows and vendors

Carlos / Vanessa — adding the technical detail asked for: 

- Routing and cache: For Redwood Hosted we route by policy; traffic originating from EU customers is preferentially routed to eu-west compute but may failover to us-west per SLA fallback. For Medra's production profile we recommend Dedicated or Private to pin region and avoid automatic failover. 

- KV cache and logs: Inference KV cache entries do not contain raw PII (we strip identifiers at the ingress when configured by controller policies). Operational logs include request identifiers and telemetry; the sample export contains hashed identifiers and timestamps only. We can provide an export pipeline that redacts or tokenizes fields to satisfy your DPIA.

- SCCs and subprocessors: The SCC extract includes our subprocessors list; we identify the data transfer roles and subprocessors located in the US and APAC. We can provide a signed subprocessors addendum if you need per-subprocessor evidence.

- Support for DPIA mitigation: If Medra needs, Redwood can produce a short mitigation statement covering technical and organisational measures (TOMs) aligned to Article 46 controls (encryption in transit+at rest, customer key control, logging minimization, contractually constrained subprocessors).

Proposed timeline: review attached PDFs today; we can provide redacted fuller logs by end of day tomorrow. If Medra prefers, we can arrange an engineer-led call to walk through the flow diagram and confirm where pseudonymization happens.

—Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@medra.tech>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com
Cc: DataPrivacy@medra.tech; liam.oconnor@medra.tech
Date: 2028-03-22T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: TIA — verification of controller data flows and vendors

Thanks Vanessa, Rishi — received and skimmed the materials. The diagram and SCC extract are helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we loop in legal and finish our DPIA: 

- Can you confirm whether the Private deployment keeps any metadata about customer region routing in a Redwood-managed control plane located outside our VPC? We need to confirm zero exposure to US-based control-plane logs for the Medra EU tenancy.
- If we take Dedicated but not Private, are there any default subcontractors involved in telemetry exports we should flag?

If you can answer those two points and provide the redacted logs you mentioned by tomorrow EOD, we should be able to close the DPIA gating questions and move to procurement. Also please include a contact for SOC 2 evidence if legal requests the latest audit letter.

I can join a short call tomorrow 09:00 CET if that helps.

Regards,
Carlos
Privacy Lead, Medra Health
